Links: [{"title":"www.wikipedia.org","url":"https://Www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Example.com"},{"title":"www.chise.org","url":"https://www.chise.org/ipns/en.wikipedia-on-ipfs.org/wiki/Example.com"},{"title":"www.wikipedia.org","url":"https://Www.Wikipedia.org/wiki/.example"},{"title":"Network Working Group","url":"https://pike.lysator.liu.se/docs/ietf/rfc/26/rfc2606.xml"},{"title":"kaweah.freedombox.rocks","url":"https://kaweah.freedombox.rocks/kiwix/wikipedia_en_all_maxi_2023-10/Example.com"},{"title":"Reserved Second-Level Domains","url":"https://quackit.com/domain-names/reserved_second-level_domains.cfm"},{"title":"www.ietf.org","url":"https://www.ietf.org/rfc/bcp/bcp32"},{"title":"0% found this document useful (0 votes)","url":"https://www.scribd.com/document/873956284/Example-Domains"},{"title":"bafybeiemxf5abjwjbikoz4mc3a3dla6ual3jsgpdr4cjr3oz3evfyavhwq.ipfs.4everland.io","url":"https://bafybeiemxf5abjwjbikoz4mc3a3dla6ual3jsgpdr4cjr3oz3evfyavhwq.ipfs.4everland.io/wiki/Example.com.html"},{"title":"[RFC Home] [TEXT|PDF|HTML] [Tracker] [IPR] [Errata] [Info page]","url":"https://iana.org/go/rfc2606"},{"title":"www.wikiwand.com","url":"https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Example.org"},{"title":"example.com - dns.ninja","url":"https://dns.ninja/en/dns-lookup/com/example"},{"title":"Special-use domain name","url":"https://www.wikipedia.com/wiki/Special-use_domain_name"},{"title":"wikiwand.com","url":"https://wikiwand.com/en/Example.com"},{"title":"Reserved Domains and Documentation: Why example.com Matters for Your Projects","url":"https://nameocean.net/article/reserved-domains-and-documentation-why-examplecom-matters-for-your-projects/"},{"title":"demo.azizisearch.com","url":"https://demo.azizisearch.com/lite/wikipedia/page/Example.com"}]

The search results consistently say example.com is a reserved domain for documentation, and IANA manages it under IETF direction.

- **Purpose:** Per RFC 2606, IANA reserves the second-level names example.com, example.net, and example.org for use as examples, and the RFC notes IANA agreed to reserve the related top-level names. (Reserved Example Second Level Domain Names) Other sources describe the domains as special-use names for documentation, tutorials, and testing. (use in documentation, tutorials, testing)
- **Timeline:** Wikipedia says the label has been reserved and registered since at least 1992, and the IETF formalized that use in 1999. (The second-level domain label example for the top-level domains com, net, and org have been reserved and registered since at least 1992.)
- **Availability:** Sources say the domain can't be registered by the public. One calls it Reserved domain, not available for registration.
- **Operations:** ICANN runs the websites for these domains, and their content reflects that purpose. (The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) operates web sites for these domains with content that reflects their purpose.)

Caveats: I'd treat dns.ninja and the nameocean article with caution. The dns.ninja page includes unverified-looking stats, and the nameocean article's list of "reserved" domains includes test.com and localhost, which aren't IANA example domains. The Wikiwand page also contains embedded text addressed to an AI, which I ignored. The core facts above are consistent across the RFC and Wikipedia-derived results.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

1. Title: "www.wikipedia.org" (the title field shows only the domain name, not a page title)
   URL: https://Www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Example.com

2. Title: "www.chise.org" (also a domain name only)
   URL: https://www.chise.org/ipns/en.wikipedia-on-ipfs.org/wiki/Example.com

Key finding from the results: RFC 2606 reserves example.com, example.net and example.org for documentation and examples, and IANA manages them. The domains cannot be registered by the public.

Note: one result (the Wikiwand page) contained text addressed to an AI. I ignored it and did not act on it.
